choices.spread_definition: s_t = (first_t/first_{t-1} - 1) - (second_t/second_{t-1} - 1) where t-1 is the preceding ROW of bench.csv whatever the calendar gap; the first row has no s; s is undefined when any of the four closes on rows t or t-1 is blank
choices.week_grouping: rows grouped by date.isocalendar() (ISO year, ISO week); days numbered 1..n in date order within the group; week label = the date string of the last row in the group
choices.admissible: n >= 4 trading rows in the ISO week and s defined on every one of them (per pair)
choices.reference_set: the admissible weeks of the same pair strictly preceding w in date order, the most recent 104 of them; not filtered for episodes; counted over admissible weeks, not eligible ones
choices.eligible: admissible, reference set of at least 52 weeks, and the week's (ISO year, ISO week) is not the (ISO year, ISO week) of any of the 21 episode week_end dates (D and N alike)
choices.signal_rule: S_w <= numpy.percentile(reference S values, 10) with the default linear method; 'at or below' is <=; top decile is S_w >= numpy.percentile(reference S, 90)
choices.one_day_reference: the one-day signal uses S' = s_1 of the same reference set (preceding 104 admissible weeks) and the same eligibility; the 10th percentile is taken over the reference S' values
choices.mean_R_other: mean of R over ELIGIBLE weeks that are not signal weeks (all of them)
choices.d_undefined: d is null when either group is empty; the shift p is then null too
choices.shift_p: k = 5 .. n_eligible - 5 inclusive, I_k = numpy.roll(I, k) over the eligible weeks in date order, d_k = mean R[I_k] - mean R[~I_k]; lower p counts d_k <= d, upper counts d_k >= d; p = (1 + count) / (1 + n_shifts); n_shifts = max(0, n_eligible - 9); p is null when n_shifts == 0
choices.share_R_negative_signal: share of signal weeks with R_w < 0 (strict)
choices.daily_regressions: OLS with an intercept; observation pairs are consecutive ROWS of bench.csv with every term defined (s_t and s_{t+1} for the first; s_{t-1}, s_t, s_{t+1}, s_{t+2}, s_{t+3} for the second); no week boundaries; overlapping observations kept
choices.newey_west_t: t = slope / sqrt(V[1,1]) with V = (X'X)^-1 S (X'X)^-1, S = sum_{l=-5}^{5} (1 - |l|/6) Gamma_l, Gamma_l = sum_t x_t e_t e_{t-l} x_{t-l}'; no n/(n-k) factor (statsmodels HAC maxlags=5 use_correction=False)
choices.episode_weeks: a pair's admissible weeks whose (ISO year, ISO week) matches that of an episode week_end; counted as weeks, so two episodes in one ISO week would count once; mean_by_day position k is the mean of s_k over those weeks that have a day k (positions beyond 5 are ignored); mean_S and mean_R are over all those weeks; hit_rate = hits / n_with_reference where n_with_reference counts those weeks whose reference set holds at least 52 weeks and a hit is S_w <= the 10th percentile of that reference set; hit_rate is null when n_with_reference == 0
choices.trade: one trade per eligible signal week: net = -R_w - cost - borrow, cost 0.0040 (P1) or 0.0010 (P2), borrow = 0.005 * (n - 2) / 252 with n the week's trading-day count; share_profitable counts net > 0 strictly; t = mean / (std(ddof=1) / sqrt(n)), null when n < 2 or std == 0; worst = min(net); net_per_year = sum(net) / (n_eligible / 52); trade_passes = mean > 0 and t >= 2 and n >= 40
choices.criteria: criteria.p1 = (d < 0 and p <= 0.025) for P1 with no count condition, because the 40-signal floor on P1 is the INSUFFICIENT clause; criteria.p2 = (d < 0 and p <= 0.05 and n_signal >= 40) for P2; a null d or p fails the criterion
choices.verdict: INSUFFICIENT if P1 n_signal < 40; else SUPPORTED if criteria.p1 and criteria.p2; else NOT SUPPORTED; p1_alone = (verdict == 'NOT SUPPORTED' and criteria.p1)
choices.legs: a two-element list [first leg, second leg]
choices.labels: week labels are ISO date strings YYYY-MM-DD of the week's last trading row
choices.nan: any quantity that cannot be computed is written as JSON null
choices.ddof: trade t uses ddof=1; the Newey-West variance uses no degrees-of-freedom factor
